validity.researcher_notes: TRACED THE ORIGIN. The gem.wiki page for this row cites exactly one source: OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, p.75 (the live opec.org PDF link is now dead — 302s to the OPEC homepage, returns an HTML shell, so it is both generic and rotted). I recovered the actual table from the ASB2013 Wayback snapshot: Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2012'. That single OPEC table is the origin of the ENTIRE GEM Saudi gas operating roster (every roster row maps 1:1 to a line there; lengths are in MILES, GEM converted to km). Critically, the table lists 'Haradh Khuff/Hawiyah | Saudi Aramco | 27 | 30' THREE TIMES consecutively, byte-identical (same length, same diameter, no capacity, no distinguishing attribute). GEM faithfully split those three identical rows into P1917 ('), P1918 ('2') and P1919 ('3') — the '2' suffix is a GEM-assigned label, not an OPEC name. Consequence: P1918 has NO independent basis as a pipeline distinct from P1917/P1919. Its sole support is one of three indistinguishable repetitions in a single source. These may be three genuine parallel Khuff-gas loops (Aramco routinely builds parallel loops), or the OPEC table simply repeated the row — I could not find any independent source (Aramco, MEED, Zawya, Argaam, trade press) that separately attests to three parallel Haradh Khuff->Hawiyah lines or that names a discrete '#2'. So this is flagged for human de-dup, not auto-resolved.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet has StartLocation blank and End='Al Hawiyah' with EndState/Province='Makkah'. That province is WRONG. Independent sources (Saudipedia; OGJ/Arab News coverage of the 2007 Haradh gas-pipeline explosion; the Ghawar geography) place the Hawiyah Gas Plant — which recovers non-associated Khuff/Jawf sour gas — in the Eastern Province, in the Hawiyah sector of the Ghawar field (~24.80N, 49.39E), NOT in the Makkah region. 'Al Hawiyah' + Makkah appears to be a conflation with the Taif-area town of Al Hawiyah / the separate Madrakah-Al Hawiyah line (P3961). OPEC's Table 4.10 names the endpoints 'Haradh Khuff' -> 'Hawiyah', i.e. from the Haradh Khuff gas area (southern Ghawar) to the Hawiyah gas plant — both Eastern Province. The 2007 explosion (an Aramco Khuff-gas line 'near Haradh gas plant, ~30 km off the Hawiyah gas plant') independently confirms real Haradh<->Hawiyah Khuff-gas trunk infrastructure exists.

routes.start_name: Haradh Khuff gas gathering area, southern Ghawar (near Haradh Gas Plant), Eastern Province
routes.end_name: Hawiyah Gas Plant, Hawiyah sector of Ghawar, Eastern Province
routes.corridor_desc: Runs north/north-east through the southern-to-central Ghawar field in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, from the Haradh Khuff non-associated-gas area up to the Hawiyah gas plant. OPEC gives 27 mi (~43 km); note the straight-line distance from Haradh TOWN (24.14,49.07) to the Hawiyah plant (24.80,49.39) is ~78 km, longer than 43 km — so the true 'Haradh Khuff' start is a Khuff-gas gathering point roughly 40 km south of the Hawiyah plant (consistent with the 2007 explosion being 'near Haradh gas plant, ~30 km off the Hawiyah gas plant'), not Haradh town itself. Corridor is therefore well-bounded (southern Ghawar, Eastern Province) but the exact endpoints are not pinned to meters.
routes.researcher_notes: End (Hawiyah Gas Plant) is well-sourced to the Hawiyah sector of Ghawar, Eastern Province (~24.80N,49.39E from the Hawiyah gas field/plant). Start coord uses Haradh town (24.14,49.07, well-established) as a defensible anchor but is flagged approximate/too-far-south per the 43 km length; no independent source pins the exact Khuff-gas gathering start, so lat/lon there is approximate not surveyed. No coordinates fabricated — both are tied to named, sourced places; corridor confidence is low because exact endpoints and the routing are not independently mapped.

summary: P1918 traces solely to one OPEC ASB table that lists 'Haradh Khuff/Hawiyah' 3x identically (=P1917/18/19): duplicate + attribution (EndProvince 'Makkah' wrong -> Eastern Province) concerns; specs (43km/30in/Aramco/gas) confirmed single-source medium; capacity unresolved.
